Add a "how to read this chart" explainer to a plot

Source: R/annotate.R
lap_annotate_howto.Rd

Places a short explainer either in plot.caption (default) or as an on-panel corner box. The lap_plot_map builders call this for their default annotate = "caption"; call it directly to override placement or add an explainer to a plot the builders did not make.

Usage

lap_annotate_howto(
  plot,
  key = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  placement = c("caption", "callout"),
  corner = c("bottom-right", "bottom-left", "top-right", "top-left"),
  lang = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  tokens = NULL
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot object.

key

Builder name without the lap_plot_ prefix (e.g. "hex_map"), used to look up the registry string. Ignored if text is given.

text

Explainer text (may contain <span> markup for ggtext). NULL (default) uses lap_howto(key).

placement

"caption" (append to plot.caption) or "callout" (an on-panel box).

corner

For "callout": which corner. One of "bottom-right" (default), "bottom-left", "top-right", "top-left".

lang, variant

Passed to lap_howto() when text is NULL.

tokens

A lap_tokens() list; computed from variant if NULL.

Value

plot with the annotation added.

See also

lap_howto(), lap_plot_map

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)
data(germany_hex_sample, package = "lapidary")
lap_plot_hex_map(germany_hex_sample, mean_gwl, annotate = NA) |>
  lap_annotate_howto("hex_map", placement = "callout")
} # }
